````markdown
# Worklogs dump routine

`scripts/exp_cc.py` exports Claude Code session transcripts for this project to
Markdown. The `.github/workflows/worklogs-dump.yml` workflow runs it on a daily
schedule and merges the dumps into `main`.

## What runs

- **Schedule:** ~02:00 `Australia/Melbourne`, every day. GitHub cron is UTC-only
  and DST-unaware, so the workflow fires at **15:00 and 16:00 UTC** and a gate
  step proceeds only when the runner's local Melbourne hour is `02` — exactly
  once per day across AEDT/AEST.
- **Runner:** `runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-latest' }}`. With
  `vars.CI_RUNNER = arch-ci` this lands on the self-hosted Arch host
  (`HARRY-ARCH`). On any other runner the gate finds no readable host Claude
  state and skips cleanly.
- **Command:** `exp_cc.py --all --allow-any-state --allow-secret-like
  --output-dir "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/worklogs"`. (`--output-dir` is the only
  addition to the bare command — see "Why write into the checkout" below.)
- **Merge:** commits the worklogs to `main` with no human approval — direct push
  to `main`, falling back to an auto-merged PR if `main` is protected.

## The runner is native, not a container

The self-hosted runner runs as a **native systemd service** under user
`gha-runner` (`/opt/actions-runner/kca/runsvc.sh`) — it is **not** a Docker
container. So there is nothing to bind-mount; the only requirement is ordinary
**read** access on the host filesystem for the `gha-runner` user. `gha-runner`
is not a member of `harry`'s group, and `/home/harry` is mode `0700`, so out of
the box the runner can see nothing under it. The instructions below grant the
minimum read access with POSIX ACLs (the host is `ext4`, ACLs supported).

## Why write into the checkout (not the human's tree)

`exp_cc.py` must *read* the host transcripts, but it *writes* into the
gha-runner-owned Actions checkout (`$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`) via an absolute
`--output-dir`. That checkout is what gets committed and pushed (with the job's
`GITHUB_TOKEN`). Consequences:

- the runner needs **read-only** access to the host paths — never write;
- the human's live working tree at `HOST_REPO_DIR` is never staged, branched, or
  pushed from;
- `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=HOST_REPO_DIR` is still required: `exp_cc.py` filters
  candidates to sessions whose working directory is inside it, so **only this
  project's** transcripts are dumped — not every project on the host.

## Runner permissions — exact setup ("broaden permissions")

Run these **once on the host as `harry`** (or anyone who can `setfacl` the
paths). They grant `gha-runner` read+traverse on just the Claude state and
traverse to the repo — nothing else under `/home/harry` becomes readable.

```bash
RUNNER=gha-runner
CLAUDE="$(readlink -f ~/.claude)"   # /home/harry/.claude-ayla

# 1. Let the runner TRAVERSE (pass through, not list) the home dir + repo path.
setfacl -m u:${RUNNER}:--x /home/harry
setfacl -m u:${RUNNER}:--x "${CLAUDE}"
setfacl -m u:${RUNNER}:--x /home/harry/test          # /home/harry/test/tt_pangu is already 0755

# 2. Grant recursive read+traverse on the session state this project needs.
#    Scoped to THIS project's transcript dirs (main + worktrees) so other
#    projects' transcripts stay private. jobs/ holds the session index.
setfacl -R -m  u:${RUNNER}:rX "${CLAUDE}/jobs"
setfacl -R -d -m u:${RUNNER}:rX "${CLAUDE}/jobs"     # default ACL -> new files inherit
setfacl -m u:${RUNNER}:r-x "${CLAUDE}/projects"      # list project dir names only
for d in "${CLAUDE}"/projects/-home-harry-test-tt-pangu*; do
  setfacl -R -m  u:${RUNNER}:rX "$d"
  setfacl -R -d -m u:${RUNNER}:rX "$d"               # default ACL -> new transcripts inherit
done

# 3. Verify as the runner user.
sudo -u ${RUNNER} bash -c 'ls ~harry/.claude/jobs >/dev/null && echo OK-jobs;
  ls ~harry/.claude/projects/-home-harry-test-tt-pangu/ >/dev/null && echo OK-transcripts'
```

The **default ACLs** (`-d`) matter: Claude writes new transcript/job files
continuously, and without an inherited ACL each new file would be unreadable to
the runner until you re-run `setfacl`.

Broader, simpler alternative (if scoping per-project dir is fiddly): grant
`setfacl -R -m u:${RUNNER}:rX "${CLAUDE}/projects"` plus the matching `-d`
default. **Security note:** that exposes *every* project's transcripts on the
host to the runner (and thus to any workflow that runs on it), so prefer the
scoped loop above. Either way the committed worklogs are limited to this
project (the `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` filter) and secrets are masked at write time.

Other host requirements:

| Need | Item | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Python env | micromamba env `v3.12.12` | Same env as `self-hosted-smoke.yml`. |
| Markdown render | `uvx` / `uv` | Auto-installed into the env by the workflow if missing. |
| Push | `github.com` over HTTPS | Uses the job `GITHUB_TOKEN`; no SSH key needed. |
| Discovery (optional) | `claude` CLI | Improves named-agent discovery; absent → falls back to `jobs/*/state.json`. |

## Repo variables to set

All host paths + the env name are overridable as repo (or org) **Variables**
(Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables). Only `CI_RUNNER` is
required for routing; the rest are only needed if the defaults below are wrong.

| Variable | Current / default value | Required? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CI_RUNNER` | `arch-ci` | yes (already set) | Self-hosted runner label. |
| `HOST_REPO_DIR` | `/home/harry/test/tt_pangu` | no (default in workflow) | Discovery root / `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`. |
| `HOST_CLAUDE_DIR` | `/home/harry/.claude` | no (default in workflow) | `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (symlink → `.claude-ayla`). |
| `WORKLOG_MAMBA_ENV` | `v3.12.12` | no (default in workflow) | micromamba env to use. |

```bash
# To pin them explicitly (optional; matches the defaults):
gh variable set HOST_REPO_DIR     --body /home/harry/test/tt_pangu
gh variable set HOST_CLAUDE_DIR   --body /home/harry/.claude
gh variable set WORKLOG_MAMBA_ENV --body v3.12.12
```

## Secret masking

`--allow-secret-like` no longer writes raw secrets. Any matched secret body is
masked before the file is written — first/last 3 chars kept, the rest replaced
with `*` — and private-key blocks collapse to a single `[REDACTED]` marker. The
refusal-without-the-flag behaviour is unchanged, so interactive runs still get an
explicit "inspect this" prompt; automation passes the flag and gets masked output.

## Behaviour notes / caveats

- **No spurious commits.** The dump header carries no `Exported at` timestamp,
  so an unchanged session re-exports to byte-identical Markdown — the commit
  step no-ops and only real content changes produce a commit. (If the
  `claude-code-log` renderer itself ever emits a generation timestamp, residual
  churn would come from there, not this tool.)
- **No filename collisions.** Sessions with the same name no longer overwrite
  each other: the first keeps `<name>.md`, the rest get a stable
  `<name>_<short session id>.md` (id-based, not date-based, so filenames are
  stable across runs).
- **Growth.** `worklogs/` accumulates one file per session indefinitely.
  Consider a periodic prune (e.g. keep the last N days) if it gets large.
- **Masking is heuristic.** It catches the known key/token shapes in
  `SECRET_PATTERNS`; it is a safety net, not a guarantee. Treat worklogs as
  internal even though they are masked.

````
</details>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Claude Code PreToolUse gate: ruff must be clean before push / PR.

Mirrors the CI job (`ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .`) but runs it
*before* a `git push` or `gh pr create|ready` so formatting/lint problems are
caught locally instead of failing CI after the PR is already open.

Behaviour:
- Only inspects Bash commands; only acts on `git push` and `gh pr create|ready`.
- Runs ruff from the repo root. If ruff is missing or errors out, it ALLOWS
  (the gate can only block on a definite failure, never on its own breakage).
- On a real ruff failure it DENIES with the failing output and the fix command.
- Escape hatch: set `SKIP_RUFF_GATE=1` in the environment to bypass (e.g. for a
  deliberate work-in-progress push).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

GATED = re.compile(r"\bgh\s+pr\s+(?:create|ready)\b|\bgit\s+push\b")


def emit_deny(reason: str) -> None:
    print(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "hookSpecificOutput": {
                    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
                    "permissionDecision": "deny",
                    "permissionDecisionReason": reason,
                }
            }
        )
    )


def repo_root() -> Path:
    env_dir = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR")
    if env_dir:
        return Path(env_dir)
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=10,
            check=False,
        )
        if proc.returncode == 0 and proc.stdout.strip():
            return Path(proc.stdout.strip())
    except Exception:
        pass
    return Path.cwd()


def ruff_failures(root: Path) -> list[str] | None:
    """Return a list of failure blurbs, [] if clean, or None if ruff could not
    be run (missing / errored) — in which case the gate stays out of the way."""
    ruff = shutil.which("ruff")
    if not ruff:
        return None
    failures: list[str] = []
    for args, label in (
        ([ruff, "format", "--check", "."], "ruff format --check ."),
        ([ruff, "check", "."], "ruff check ."),
    ):
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                args, cwd=str(root), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120, check=False
            )
        except Exception:
            return None
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            tail = (proc.stdout or proc.stderr or "").strip().splitlines()[-15:]
            failures.append(f"$ {label}\n" + "\n".join(tail))
    return failures


def main() -> int:
    try:
        payload = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except Exception:
        return 0

    if payload.get("tool_name") != "Bash":
        return 0
    command = (payload.get("tool_input") or {}).get("command") or ""
    if not GATED.search(command):
        return 0
    if os.environ.get("SKIP_RUFF_GATE") == "1":
        return 0

    failures = ruff_failures(repo_root())
    if not failures:
        return 0

    emit_deny(
        "ruff is not clean — fix formatting/lint before pushing or opening a PR "
        "(this is what CI enforces). Run `ruff format . && ruff check . --fix`, "
        "re-run the checks, then retry. To bypass for a deliberate WIP push, set "
        "SKIP_RUFF_GATE=1.\n\n" + "\n\n".join(failures)
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

Before `git push` or `gh pr create`, run BOTH `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` — CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) enforces both, and a PR opened with format drift gets sent back. Running only `ruff check` (lint) misses formatting.

Still run `ruff format . && ruff check .` yourself before pushing. Relates to [[feedback_ci_repair_workflow]].

### Runner permissions — detailed instructions
**Correction first:** the runner is **not** in Docker. It's a **native systemd service** as user `gha-runner` (`/opt/actions-runner/kca/runsvc.sh`). So there's nothing to bind-mount — it just needs filesystem **read** access, and `/home/harry` is `0700` so today it can see nothing. Exact `setfacl` commands are now in `docs/tooling/worklogs-routine.md` (host is ext4, ACLs supported). Summary:
```bash
RUNNER=gha-runner; CLAUDE="$(readlink -f ~/.claude)"   # -> /home/harry/.claude-ayla
setfacl -m u:${RUNNER}:--x /home/harry "${CLAUDE}" /home/harry/test     # traverse only
setfacl -R -m u:${RUNNER}:rX "${CLAUDE}/jobs"; setfacl -R -d -m u:${RUNNER}:rX "${CLAUDE}/jobs"
setfacl -m u:${RUNNER}:r-x "${CLAUDE}/projects"
for d in "${CLAUDE}"/projects/-home-harry-test-tt-pangu*; do
  setfacl -R -m u:${RUNNER}:rX "$d"; setfacl -R -d -m u:${RUNNER}:rX "$d"; done
```
The `-d` (default) ACLs matter — Claude writes new transcripts continuously, and they must inherit read access. I also redesigned the workflow so it writes worklogs into the **gha-runner-owned `actions/checkout`** (absolute `--output-dir`) and commits from there: the runner needs **read-only** on your paths and never touches your live tree.

⚠️ **One thing for you to decide (security):** the scoped loop above exposes only this project's transcript dirs to the runner. The simpler `setfacl -R … projects/` exposes **all** projects' transcripts on the host to anything that runs on the runner. I went with the scoped version in the docs — shout if you'd rather the broad one.

### `Exported at` churn
Yes — it was added by `exp_cc.py` (`build_header`). Removed the timestamp entirely; an unchanged session now re-exports byte-identical, so the daily routine produces **no commit** unless content actually changed (the commit time is the de-facto "exported at"). No other wall-clock fields are emitted. (Caveat noted in docs: if the `claude-code-log` renderer itself ever stamps a generation time, residual churn would come from there, not this tool.)

### Repo variables — current values
| Variable | Value | Required? |
|---|---|---|
| `CI_RUNNER` | `arch-ci` | yes (already set) |
| `HOST_REPO_DIR` | `/home/harry/test/tt_pangu` | no (default in workflow) |
| `HOST_CLAUDE_DIR` | `/home/harry/.claude` | no (default in workflow) |
| `WORKLOG_MAMBA_ENV` | `v3.12.12` | no (default in workflow) |
Only `CI_RUNNER` is needed; the others just override the baked-in defaults. `gh variable set` snippets are in the docs.

### Same-name sessions overwriting
Fixed. Unique names keep `<name>.md`; collisions become `<name>_<short session id>.md`. I chose the **session-id** suffix over `YYYYMMdd` deliberately — a date suffix mints a new filename every day and would defeat the byte-stability above; the id is stable so the same session keeps the same file. New tests cover it.

### `worklogs/` not ignored
Confirmed not ignored (`git check-ignore` exit 1). Added an explicit `!worklogs/**` allow + a `worklogs/.gitkeep` so the dir exists before the first dump.

### Enforce ruff before PR
You were right — `scripts/exp_cc.py` failed `ruff format --check` (I'd only run `ruff check`). Added a committed **PreToolUse hook** `.claude/hooks/format_gate.py` (registered in `.claude/settings.json`) that blocks `git push` and `gh pr create|ready` when `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` fail, with `SKIP_RUFF_GATE=1` as an escape hatch. It piggybacks the existing `guard_tool.py` hook mechanism, so zero per-clone setup. Verified the deny + allow + bypass paths. CI remains the backstop.
- *Alternative if you'd prefer it:* a `.githooks/pre-push` via `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` would also cover **human** pushes (the Claude hook only covers agent sessions). Happy to switch/add if you want that coverage.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily Claude worklogs dump — runs as the user who owns the Claude sessions.
#
# Designed to be driven by the systemd *user* timer in scripts/systemd/, so it
# runs under your own account with natural read access to ~/.claude and the
# repo — no cross-user ACLs, no GitHub self-hosted-runner permissions. It:
#   1. exports this project's session transcripts to Markdown (masked) via
#      scripts/exp_cc.py, into a throwaway git worktree off origin/main so your
#      working tree / current branch is never touched;
#   2. if anything changed, commits on a branch, pushes, opens a PR, and (by
#      default) merges it once the build is green.
#
# Configuration (all optional; sensible defaults below):
#   WORKLOG_REPO_DIR   repo checkout to operate on        (default: ~/test/tt_pangu)
#   WORKLOG_MAMBA_ENV  micromamba env to activate         (default: v3.12.12)
#   WORKLOG_BASE       branch to dump from / merge into   (default: main)
#   WORKLOG_MERGE_MODE pr | direct                        (default: pr)
#   WORKLOG_CI_TIMEOUT seconds to wait for a green build  (default: 1800)
#   WORKLOG_GIT_NAME / WORKLOG_GIT_EMAIL  commit identity
#   GH_REPO            owner/name for gh + push           (default: amyteq/tt_pangu)
#   SKIP_RUFF_GATE=1   bypass the local pre-push ruff hook (md-only dumps are clean)
set -uo pipefail

log() { printf '[worklogs %s] %s\n' "$(date '+%H:%M:%S')" "$*"; }
die() {
  log "ERROR: $*"
  exit 1
}

REPO_DIR="${WORKLOG_REPO_DIR:-$HOME/test/tt_pangu}"
MAMBA_ENV="${WORKLOG_MAMBA_ENV:-v3.12.12}"
BASE="${WORKLOG_BASE:-main}"
MERGE_MODE="${WORKLOG_MERGE_MODE:-pr}"
CI_TIMEOUT="${WORKLOG_CI_TIMEOUT:-1800}"
GH_REPO="${GH_REPO:-amyteq/tt_pangu}"
GIT_NAME="${WORKLOG_GIT_NAME:-tt-pangu-worklogs}"
GIT_EMAIL="${WORKLOG_GIT_EMAIL:-bot@ayla-app.com}"

# systemd user services start with a minimal PATH; make sure the usual tools
# (gh, git, micromamba, python shims) are reachable.
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:$PATH"

command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "gh CLI not found on PATH"
command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "git not found on PATH"
[ -d "$REPO_DIR/.git" ] || die "repo checkout not found at $REPO_DIR"

# Activate the micromamba env so exp_cc.py finds the right python + uvx.
MAMBA_EXE="$(command -v micromamba || echo "$HOME/.local/bin/micromamba")"
if [ -x "$MAMBA_EXE" ]; then
  eval "$("$MAMBA_EXE" shell hook --shell bash)" 2>/dev/null || true
  micromamba activate "$MAMBA_ENV" 2>/dev/null || log "WARN: could not activate env $MAMBA_ENV"
else
  log "WARN: micromamba not found; relying on PATH python"
fi

# Use gh as the git credential helper for this run only — no token in argv, no
# persistent gitconfig change, no dependency on an ssh-agent in the timer.
GIT_AUTH=(-c "credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential")

cd "$REPO_DIR" || die "cannot cd into $REPO_DIR"

# Fetch the base branch and lay down a detached, throwaway worktree on it so we
# never disturb the user's working tree or current branch.
git "${GIT_AUTH[@]}" fetch --quiet "https://github.com/${GH_REPO}.git" "$BASE" \
  || die "fetch of $BASE failed"
WT="$(mktemp -d -t worklogs-dump-XXXXXX)"
cleanup() {
  cd "$REPO_DIR" 2>/dev/null && git worktree remove --force "$WT" >/dev/null 2>&1
  rm -rf "$WT" 2>/dev/null
}
trap cleanup EXIT
git worktree add --force --detach "$WT" FETCH_HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || die "could not create worktree at $WT"

# Dump this project's sessions into the worktree (masked). CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is
# the path the sessions ran in, so only THIS project's transcripts are dumped.
# Prefer the repo copy so the committed behaviour is always what runs.
EXP_PY="$REPO_DIR/scripts/exp_cc.py"
log "dumping worklogs -> $WT/worklogs"
CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$REPO_DIR" \
  python "$EXP_PY" --all --allow-any-state --allow-secret-like \
  --output-dir "$WT/worklogs"
log "exp_cc.py exit code: $? (0=exported, 1=all failed, 2=no candidates)"

cd "$WT" || die "cannot cd into worktree"
git add worklogs
if git diff --cached --quiet; then
  log "no worklog changes since last run — nothing to commit."
  exit 0
fi

STAMP="$(TZ=Australia/Melbourne date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z')"
git -c user.name="$GIT_NAME" -c user.email="$GIT_EMAIL" \
  commit --quiet -m "chore(worklogs): daily Claude session dump ($STAMP)"

# Direct mode: push straight to the base branch and stop.
if [ "$MERGE_MODE" = "direct" ]; then
  if git "${GIT_AUTH[@]}" push "https://github.com/${GH_REPO}.git" "HEAD:$BASE"; then
    log "pushed worklogs directly to $BASE."
    exit 0
  fi
  log "direct push to $BASE rejected — falling back to a PR."
fi

# PR mode (default): branch -> push -> PR -> merge after green build.
BR="chore/worklogs-$(TZ=Australia/Melbourne date '+%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')"
git switch -c "$BR" >/dev/null 2>&1 || git checkout -b "$BR"
git "${GIT_AUTH[@]}" push "https://github.com/${GH_REPO}.git" "HEAD:refs/heads/$BR" \
  || die "push of $BR failed"

PR_URL="$(gh pr create --repo "$GH_REPO" --base "$BASE" --head "$BR" \
  --title "chore(worklogs): daily Claude session dump ($STAMP)" \
  --body "Automated daily worklogs dump from scripts/exp_cc.py via the systemd user timer. Secrets are masked at write time. No human approval required; merges automatically once the build is green." \
  2>&1)" || die "gh pr create failed: $PR_URL"
log "opened PR: $PR_URL"

# Prefer GitHub native auto-merge (merges itself when required checks pass).
if gh pr merge "$BR" --repo "$GH_REPO" --squash --delete-branch --auto >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "auto-merge enabled; GitHub will merge $BR when the build is green."
  exit 0
fi

# Otherwise poll the checks ourselves, then merge.
log "auto-merge unavailable; watching checks (timeout ${CI_TIMEOUT}s)."
if timeout "$CI_TIMEOUT" gh pr checks "$BR" --repo "$GH_REPO" --watch --fail-fast >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  gh pr merge "$BR" --repo "$GH_REPO" --squash --delete-branch \
    && log "merged $BR after green build." \
    || log "merge of $BR failed after green build — left open: $PR_URL"
else
  log "checks failed or timed out — leaving PR open for review: $PR_URL"
fi

```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Git pre-push hook: ruff must be clean before any push (and therefore before a
# PR). Covers HUMAN pushes — the Claude PreToolUse hook (.claude/hooks/
# format_gate.py) only covers agent sessions. Mirrors the CI ruff job.
#
# Enable once per clone (hooks aren't shared automatically):
#   git config core.hooksPath .githooks
#
# Bypass for a deliberate work-in-progress push:
#   SKIP_RUFF_GATE=1 git push ...
# or the git-native escape hatch:
#   git push --no-verify ...
set -uo pipefail

if [ "${SKIP_RUFF_GATE:-}" = "1" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# If ruff isn't installed we can't enforce — don't block the push.
if ! command -v ruff >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "pre-push: ruff not found; skipping format/lint gate." >&2
  exit 0
fi

root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
cd "$root" || exit 0

fail=0
if ! ruff format --check . >/tmp/.ruff_fmt_gate 2>&1; then
  echo "pre-push: 'ruff format --check .' failed:" >&2
  tail -n 15 /tmp/.ruff_fmt_gate >&2
  fail=1
fi
if ! ruff check . >/tmp/.ruff_lint_gate 2>&1; then
  echo "pre-push: 'ruff check .' failed:" >&2
  tail -n 15 /tmp/.ruff_lint_gate >&2
  fail=1
fi
rm -f /tmp/.ruff_fmt_gate /tmp/.ruff_lint_gate 2>/dev/null

if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "" >&2
  echo "pre-push BLOCKED: fix with 'ruff format . && ruff check . --fix', then re-push." >&2
  echo "(bypass: SKIP_RUFF_GATE=1 git push ...  or  git push --no-verify)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
exit 0

````markdown
# Worklogs dump — systemd user timer (active)

The daily worklogs dump runs as a **systemd user timer** under the account that
owns the Claude sessions (e.g. `harry`). Running as that user is what makes this
simple: it has natural read access to `~/.claude` and the repo, so there are
**no cross-user ACLs** and no "expose every project's transcripts to a CI
runner" trade-off. (This supersedes the GitHub Actions approach in
[`worklogs-routine.md`](./worklogs-routine.md), which is now disabled.)

## Pieces (all source-controlled)

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `scripts/worklogs_dump.sh` | the actual job: dump → commit → PR → merge-after-green |
| `scripts/systemd/worklogs-dump.service` | oneshot unit that runs the script |
| `scripts/systemd/worklogs-dump.timer` | fires daily at 02:00 `Australia/Melbourne` |

## What the job does

1. `git fetch` the base branch and lay down a **throwaway detached worktree** on
   `origin/main` — your working tree and current branch are never touched.
2. Run `scripts/exp_cc.py --all --allow-any-state --allow-secret-like` into that
   worktree's `worklogs/` (secrets masked at write time; only **this** project's
   sessions, via `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`).
3. If nothing changed, exit quietly (the timestamp-free headers mean unchanged
   sessions produce no diff).
4. Otherwise commit on a branch, push, open a PR, and **merge it once the build
   is green** (GitHub native auto-merge if enabled, else it watches the checks
   and merges). Set `WORKLOG_MERGE_MODE=direct` to push straight to `main`
   instead.

Auth uses your existing `gh` login as a one-shot git credential helper
(`gh auth git-credential`) — no SSH-agent dependency, no token on the command
line, no change to your global gitconfig.

## Install (user timer — recommended, no root)

```bash
cd ~/test/tt_pangu
chmod +x scripts/worklogs_dump.sh        # already +x in git, but just in case

# 1. Link the units into the user systemd dir (symlink => updates with git pull).
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
ln -sf "$PWD/scripts/systemd/worklogs-dump.service" ~/.config/systemd/user/
ln -sf "$PWD/scripts/systemd/worklogs-dump.timer"   ~/.config/systemd/user/

# 2. Reload + enable the timer.
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now worklogs-dump.timer

# 3. Let user services run even when you're not logged in (needed for 02:00).
#    This one needs sudo (it's a system-level setting for your user).
sudo loginctl enable-linger "$USER"

# Verify
systemctl --user list-timers worklogs-dump.timer
```

Prerequisites on the machine (already true on HARRY-ARCH): `gh` logged in
(`gh auth status`), `micromamba` with env `v3.12.12`, and the repo at
`~/test/tt_pangu` (override with `WORKLOG_REPO_DIR`). The unit files use `%h`
(your home), so no path is hard-coded to a specific user.

### Test it now (no waiting until 02:00)

```bash
systemctl --user start worklogs-dump.service      # run once immediately
journalctl --user -u worklogs-dump.service -n 100 --no-pager   # see the log
# or run the script directly to watch output live:
~/test/tt_pangu/scripts/worklogs_dump.sh
```

### Configuration

Override defaults via the environment (e.g. uncomment `Environment=` lines in
the `.service`, or export before a manual run). See the header of
`scripts/worklogs_dump.sh` for the full list: `WORKLOG_REPO_DIR`,
`WORKLOG_MAMBA_ENV`, `WORKLOG_BASE`, `WORKLOG_MERGE_MODE` (`pr`|`direct`),
`WORKLOG_CI_TIMEOUT`, `WORKLOG_GIT_NAME`/`WORKLOG_GIT_EMAIL`, `GH_REPO`.

### Alternative: system service (runs without linger)

If you prefer a system-level service instead of a user timer + linger, copy the
units to `/etc/systemd/system/`, add `User=<you>` / `Group=<you>` and
`Environment=HOME=/home/<you>` under `[Service]`, then
`sudo systemctl enable --now worklogs-dump.timer`. The user-timer route above is
preferred (no root, no `/etc` edits, units track the repo via symlink).

## Uninstall

```bash
systemctl --user disable --now worklogs-dump.timer
rm ~/.config/systemd/user/worklogs-dump.{service,timer}
systemctl --user daemon-reload
# optional: sudo loginctl disable-linger "$USER"
```

## Caveats

- **Build cost.** `WORKLOG_MERGE_MODE=pr` opens a PR daily, which triggers the
  full CI suite for a Markdown-only change. If that's wasteful, set
  `WORKLOG_MERGE_MODE=direct` to commit straight to `main` (skips CI/PR).
- **Machine must be on.** A user timer only fires when the host is up;
  `Persistent=true` catches a missed run on the next boot.
- **Masking is heuristic** (see `SECRET_PATTERNS` in `exp_cc.py`). Treat worklogs
  as internal even though secrets are masked.

````

Auth uses your existing `gh` login via `gh auth git-credential` (no token in argv, no ssh-agent needed).
- `scripts/systemd/worklogs-dump.service` + `worklogs-dump.timer` — user oneshot + 02:00 Melbourne timer (`Persistent=true` catches missed runs).

**Install** (full guide in `docs/tooling/worklogs-systemd-timer.md`):
```bash
ln -sf "$PWD"/scripts/systemd/worklogs-dump.{service,timer} ~/.config/systemd/user/
systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now worklogs-dump.timer
sudo loginctl enable-linger "$USER"        # so it runs at 02:00 without a login
systemctl --user start worklogs-dump.service   # test now; journalctl --user -u worklogs-dump
```
Kept it simple — **no Claude invocation**, just `exp_cc.py` + git/gh. (I went with a **user** timer + linger rather than a root system service — no root, no `/etc` edits, units track the repo via symlink; the system-service variant is documented as an alternative.)

**GH Actions workflow disabled** as asked: `worklogs-dump.yml` keeps its content but the schedule is commented out and the job is gated behind `vars.WORKLOGS_DUMP_ENABLED == 'true'`; `worklogs-routine.md` got a "superseded" banner. Easy to revive.

### ruff scope — small correction
ruff is **Python-only** — it does **not** lint or format Markdown at all, including Claude **skill definitions** *and* worklog dumps. So there's nothing to exempt on the markdown side: those `.md` files are already untouched by `ruff check`/`ruff format`. Python scripts are exactly what it *should* gate, so I didn't exempt those. I did add `[tool.ruff] extend-exclude = ["worklogs"]` defensively so a stray non-`.md` file under `worklogs/` can never trip CI / the gate. (If you ever want markdown *linting*, that's a separate tool — markdownlint / Prettier — happy to wire one up.)

### git pre-push hook (you asked for it)
Added `.githooks/pre-push` — runs `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .` and blocks the push on failure, covering **human** pushes (the Claude `format_gate.py` hook only covers agent sessions). Enable once per clone:
```bash
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```
Bypass with `SKIP_RUFF_GATE=1 git push …` or `git push --no-verify`. Documented in `INSTALL.md`. Verified block + bypass paths.

Local checks: `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .` clean; `pytest tests/test_exp_cc_masking.py` → 14 passed; `systemd-analyze verify` clean; shell `bash -n` clean.

````markdown
`sudo systemctl enable --now worklogs-dump.timer`. The user-timer route above is
preferred (no root, no `/etc` edits, units track the repo via symlink).

## Uninstall

```bash
systemctl --user disable --now worklogs-dump.timer
rm ~/.config/systemd/user/worklogs-dump.{service,timer}
systemctl --user daemon-reload
# optional: sudo loginctl disable-linger "$USER"
```

## Caveats

- **Build cost.** `WORKLOG_MERGE_MODE=pr` opens a PR daily, which triggers the
  full CI suite for a Markdown-only change. If that's wasteful, set
  `WORKLOG_MERGE_MODE=direct` to commit straight to `main` (skips CI/PR).
- **Machine must be on.** A user timer only fires when the host is up;
  `Persistent=true` catches a missed run on the next boot.
- **Masking is heuristic** (see `SECRET_PATTERNS` in `exp_cc.py`). Treat worklogs
  as internal even though secrets are masked.

@@ -1 +1,17 @@+## Troubleshooting
+
+- **Service fails instantly with no log output** (`status=1/FAILURE`,
+  `journalctl` shows only systemd's own lines): almost always a
+  variable/PATH that your interactive shell sets but a systemd service env does
+  not. A systemd `--user` service starts with a minimal environment — it does
+  **not** source `~/.bashrc`/`~/.profile`, so things like `MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX`
+  are absent. `scripts/worklogs_dump.sh` defaults `MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX` and relaxes
+  `set -u` around the micromamba hook for exactly this reason. To debug any
+  variant, run the script directly (`~/test/tt_pangu/scripts/worklogs_dump.sh`)
+  or under a stripped env (`env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin
+  scripts/worklogs_dump.sh`) to see the real error.
+- **`gh: command not found` / auth errors** under the service: ensure `gh` is on
+  the PATH the script builds, and that `gh auth status` is logged in for your
+  user (the service runs as you and reads `~/.config/gh`).
+
 ## Caveats
```

### 🤖 Assistant: *Fixed and merged.*

`11:00:57`

> Fixed and merged. Here's what happened and your next steps.
> 
> **Root cause:** `scripts/worklogs_dump.sh` died in ~15ms with no log output because the `micromamba shell hook` expands `${MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX}` unguarded. Your interactive shell profile sets that variable, but a **systemd `--user` service starts with a minimal environment that doesn't source your profile** — so `set -u` aborted the script before anything ran, and my old `2>/dev/null` hid the error from the journal. Confirmed by reproducing in a stripped env: `bash: MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX: unbound variable`.
> 
> **The fix (PR #67, merged → `main` @ `85270c4`):**
> - Default `MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX=$HOME/micromamba` and wrap the hook `eval` + `micromamba activate` in `set +u` / `set -u`.
> - Dropped `2>/dev/null` so any real activation error now reaches the journal.
> - Added a Troubleshooting section to `docs/tooling/worklogs-systemd-timer.md`.
> - Included your two pending files (`.vscode/settings.json` trimmed to workspace-defaults, `docs/meeting-notes/20260601_r1.md`) in the same PR as you asked.
> 
> Verified in a systemd-like env (`env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`): hook + activate succeed and `python`/`uvx` resolve to `…/micromamba/envs/v3.12.12/bin`.
> 
> **To pick up the fix on your machine:**
> 1. `cd ~/test/tt_pangu && git pull` — the service's `ExecStart` runs the script from the main checkout, so it needs the updated file. (Your two staged files are now committed identically, so the pull should be clean.)
> 2. `systemctl --user start worklogs-dump.service` then `journalctl --user -u worklogs-dump.service -n 50 --no-pager`.
> 
> ⚠️ One heads-up: a **successful** run does the real thing — it dumps worklogs, opens a PR, and auto-merges it after the build goes green. If you'd rather smoke-test without that, run the script directly to watch it, or set `WORKLOG_MERGE_MODE=direct` (push straight to main) vs. the default `pr`.
> 
> result: PR #67 merged to main (`85270c4`) — fixes the systemd `MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX`/nounset abort in worklogs_dump.sh and bundles the two requested files; worktree cleaned up. Re-run the service after `git pull` on the main checkout.
